sources.title: Morph public model metadata API
sources.evidence: The exact morph-v3-fast entry is named Morph: v3 Fast Apply, describes code-edit application, and reports text input/output with max_context_length 262144. The created value changed between fetches, so it is not reliable release-date evidence.

sources.title: Morph API documentation: Fast Apply
sources.evidence: Names morph-v3-fast and morph-v3-large separately. Fast is for quick edits; requests combine instruction, original code and an update snippet and return a merged file. The later Fast Models section covers different open-weight general models; its reasoning/tools statement is not about Apply.

sources.title: Fast Apply: Code Merging at 10,500 tok/s for AI Agents
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the introduction, Architecture section and FAQ state nominal 7B at 10,500 tok/s; the Models & Pricing table assigns that speed and $0.80/M input to exact morph-v3-fast, while morph-v3-large has a separate speed/price row. No active-parameter count or named base checkpoint is stated. This is a published nominal size, not a tensor census; marketing accuracy figures are not used.

sources.title: Morph models
sources.evidence: Lists morph-v3-fast under specialized agent models as Fast Apply (fast), separately from Fast Apply (large) and the open-source general coding model lineup. Confirms 262k context and code-edit merging.

sources.title: Morph End User License Agreement
sources.evidence: Defines software to include applicable model weights and grants restricted, revocable usage rights; prohibits redistribution and model-weight extraction. Separately identified open-source components have their own licenses. Enterprise self-hosting is licensed separately; it does not establish open weights.

sources.title: Morph Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Sections 3 and 6 describe API/private-deployment service and retained ownership of models, algorithms and software, with no license except the stated service terms. Supports proprietary classification for the Morph-owned Apply service.

sources.title: Morph Release Notes
sources.evidence: Contains dated Apply service updates but no entry establishing the first public release of the exact morph-v3-fast identifier. Product-wide updates cannot establish this variant release date.

sources.title: Optimizing Models to Be Fast at Codegen
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 in full. The June 19, 2026 research article discusses Fast Apply, trained speculators and hosted open coding models, but assigns no total/active count or named base to morph-v3-fast. Vicuna, Qwen and 80B MoE kernel examples concern other models and cannot establish Fast Apply lineage or an active-count convention.

sources.title: Speculative Decoding: Speedup, Variants, and Setup
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, including the later benchmark tables and exact production FAQ: morph-v3-fast uses n-gram prompt lookup with a 64-token draft window. Tables compare speculative-decoding speedups and acceptance rates, not activated parameters for this model. This serving technique establishes neither neural architecture nor an active count.

sources.title: Models.dev Morph V3 Fast record
sources.evidence: Current source carries July 7, 2025 and false reasoning/tools from curated OpenRouter catalog data. Its comment points to Morph API metadata for limits, but not a developer launch announcement or explicit capability classification.

sources.title: Morph V3 Fast provider catalog
sources.evidence: Lists July 7, 2025 and an 82K provider context. Useful catalog leads; neither establishes an original developer release date or overrides the direct Morph API 262144 limit.

sources.title: Fast Apply SDK component documentation
sources.evidence: Exact morph-v3-fast examples return merged code in message.content. A separate parent model calls the edit_file wrapper. The wrapper being a tool does not show that morph-v3-fast itself emits tool calls.

sources.title: Fast Apply Makes Faster Agents
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: web rendering again exposes the November 4, 2025 title, authors and table of contents but no article body; fresh direct HTTP retrieval returned 429. No training, base-model lineage or parameter count is inferred from the inaccessible body.

sources.title: About Morph: model training and deployment
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Morph describes continued pretraining, RL and specialized inference, with a separate trained model for each task. It does not identify a named Fast Apply base checkpoint or separately publish active parameters, so generic training language cannot support a base-size inference.

sources.title: Kortix Fast Apply training repository
sources.evidence: Fresh named-base search lead checked October 27: Kortix documents its own FastApply-7B/1.5B Qwen2.5-Coder fine-tunes, then separately says it uses the hosted Morph API for production. These are not identified as Morph v3 Fast weights; neither their Qwen lineage nor parameter counts transfer to this model.

name.note: Normalized display name agrees with the exact v3 Fast Apply identifier; no rename is required.

developer.note: Morph publishes and operates this own-brand Apply model; AutoInfra, Inc. is the legal entity.

family.note: Retain the catalog grouping for Morph v3 Apply models. This is not a claim of shared base architecture.

release_date.note: July 7, 2025 is a provider/catalog date. No reviewed developer announcement establishes this as the earliest release of morph-v3-fast. The API created field changes on fetch and is unsuitable. Clear the unsupported exact date.

open_weights.note: The Morph-owned Apply model is distributed under restricted service/enterprise terms, separately from the explicitly open-weight hosted lineup. Licensed self-hosting does not make the model openly distributed.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the developer-controlled model/service terms, not an invented SPDX identifier. Open-source SDK components and separately hosted open models are excluded.

parameters_b.note: Reverified developer nominal 7B. The product page states the size and maps its 10,500 tok/s and $0.80/M input offering to the exact morph-v3-fast row; the model lineup corroborates that identity. Preserve the published nominal precision without requiring a tensor census or transferring the count to Large.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh separate active-count and later research/comparison-table searches found no stated count for morph-v3-fast. Current primary metadata, docs, product/model pages and inference research do not publish one or establish named-base lineage. Kortix FastApply Qwen fine-tunes are a different project; the November article body remains unavailable. Do not infer active count from total size, speculative-decoding throughput or generic architecture examples.

architecture.note: Reviewed primary material describes serving kernels and n-gram speculative decoding but no exact-variant neural architecture. The later November article body was not retrievable. Qwen references, draft architectures and MoE kernel examples elsewhere are not exact model configuration evidence.

context_window.note: Exact token limit from Morph public API metadata, corroborated by rounded 262k on the website. Some reseller pages still list 81920; that provider limit is not used to overwrite the direct developer value. No authenticated inference test was performed.

modalities.note: Exact API entry explicitly declares text input and output; code is serialized text.

reasoning.note: Developer positions this as a merge step separate from planning/reasoning, but that does not explicitly classify exposed reasoning-mode support. No negative capability declaration was verified. Clear the catalog false rather than infer it from missing metadata.

tool_call.note: Documentation makes Apply callable by another agent as edit_file; this does not establish native tool-call generation. No explicit positive or negative classification for the exact model was verified. Clear the unsupported false.

description.value: Specialized code-edit application model that merges an instruction and proposed edit snippet into an existing source file and returns the complete updated file.
description.note: Replace unsupported assistance, extraction and routine-automation language with the documented exact-model merge function; omit inconsistent marketing accuracy figures.

patch.description: Specialized code-edit application model that merges an instruction and proposed edit snippet into an existing source file and returns the complete updated file.
patch.notes: Morph publishes nominal 7B for Fast Apply, matched to morph-v3-fast by the exact 10,500 tok/s and $0.80 row. Active parameters are not separately disclosed, and no named base lineage is established. Neural architecture remains unresolved. Morph documents 262,144 text tokens; the exact release date and native reasoning/tool support remain unverified.

sources.label: Morph speculative decoding and exact Fast production configuration

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains developer nominal 7B for exact morph-v3-fast. Separate active-count, later comparison-table and named-base searches found no support for an active count; Kortix Qwen-based FastApply is a different project, and the November Morph article body remains unavailable. Explicitly patches active parameters to null. The other 12 field assessments are preserved.
